The advisory: restrictions set with mbedtls_ssl_conf_sig_algs() (mbedtls_ssl_conf_sig_hashes() in 2.28) are not applied to certificate-chain signatures. Buddy sets no such restriction (src/connect/tls/tls.cpp never calls mbedtls_ssl_conf_sig_hashes), so the chain is verified with the default certificate profile, as intended, against the single embedded Prusa CA.

statements.action_statement: Undefine MBEDTLS_AES_ROM_TABLES (the tables then use about 2.5 KB of RAM with MBEDTLS_AES_FEWER_TABLES), or move to hardware AES.
statements.status_notes: MBEDTLS_AES_ROM_TABLES is on (include/mbedtls/cipher_config_ece.h), so the AES tables are read through the flash accelerator cache. The advisory says that short-lived TLS session keys are not at risk; the attacker needs the timing of many AES calls with one key.

statements.impact_statement: Spectre v1 side channels need speculative execution of loads and a local attacker that runs code. The Cortex-M4 (STM32F4) does not execute loads speculatively (Arm does not list Cortex-M cores as affected by Spectre), and the firmware runs no untrusted code.
